title: The Invisible Editorial Layer: Formalizing Undisclosed Inference-Time Steering, Probability Placement, and the Attribution Problem in Deployed Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2608.24662v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are commonly evaluated under the assumption that their observable behavior is primarily determined by model weights, training data, alignment procedures, and user prompts. This view is incomplete. Modern inference pipelines may systematically modify the probability distribution produced by a model immediately before token selection, creating an additional layer of control between frozen weights and observed text.   While controlled generation (e.g., PPLM, GeDi, DExperts, FUDGE) and text-watermarking systems (e.g., SynthID-Text) demonstrate the technical maturity of decoding- and logit-level interventions, the governance, security, and economic implications of an undisclosed inference policy remain comparatively underexplored. translated_title: 隐形编辑层：形式化已部署语言模型中的未公开推理时引导、概率放置与归因问题
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLMs）通常在假设其可观察行为主要由模型权重、训练数据、对齐流程和用户提示决定的前提下进行评估。这种观点是不完整的。现代推理流水线可能在令牌选择前立即系统地修改模型产生的概率分布，从而在冻结的权重和观察到的文本之间增加一个额外的控制层。虽然受控生成（例如PPLM、GeDi、DExperts、FUDGE）和文本水印系统（例如SynthID-Text）展示了解码和逻辑层干预的技术成熟度，但未公开推理策略的治理、安全和经济影响相对而言仍未得到充分探索。本文考察了推理时框架偏差的出现：即通过推理时干预系统地修改生成语言，使其偏向政治、意识形态、制度或商业框架。
tldr: 本文首次系统性地形式化了大型语言模型部署中未公开的推理时干预层，指出该层可导致生成文本产生系统性框架偏差，并提出了归因问题，为AI治理与安全提供了新的分析视角。
en_tdlr: This paper systematically formalizes the undisclosed inference-time intervention layer in deployed LLMs, revealing its potential to induce systematic framing bias in generated text and raising the attribution problem, offering a novel analytical perspective for AI governance and security.
